subject: gk
question: When was the Indian Meteorological Department,Which collects data on temperature, rainfall, wind, etc., and makes weather forecasts, established by the Government of India?
solution:
The correct answer is __**1875**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The India Meteorological Department (IMD), **established by the **Government of India in 1875**, serves as the **nation's primary National Meteorological Service**, overseeing** all meteorology-related matters**.
 
• Operating under the Ministry of Earth Sciences, IMD holds primary responsibility for meteorological observations, weather forecasting, and seismology in the country. 
 
• Headquartered in Delhi, IMD manages a vast network of observation stations spread across India and Antarctica, ensuring comprehensive coverage.
 
• Regional offices located in Chennai, Mumbai, Kolkata, Nagpur, Guwahati, and New Delhi facilitate efficient operations and localized services.
 
• Recognized as one of the six Regional Specialised Meteorological Centres by the World Meteorological Organisation, IMD plays a crucial role in forecasting and managing tropical cyclones in the Northern Indian Ocean region.
 
• This includes issuing warnings and naming cyclones affecting areas such as the Malacca Straits, the Bay of Bengal, the Arabian Sea, and the Persian Gulf.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• After India gained independence on 27 April 1949, IMD became a member of the **World Meteorological Organisation**.
 
• The agency's importance has grown significantly due to the crucial role of monsoon rains in Indian agriculture.
 
• It is instrumental in forecasting the annual monsoon and monitoring its progress across the country each season.
 
• The IMD is led by the Director General of Meteorology, presently Mrutyunjay Mohapatra.
 
• In January 2016, IMD initiated the System of Aerosol Monitoring and Research (SAMAR) to analyze the concentration of Black carbon, radiative properties of aerosols, environmental visibility, and their climatic impacts. SAMAR comprises a network of 16 aethalometers, 12 sky radiometers, and 12 nephelometers.
